structured.answer: I'd go with כלל. Its S&P 500 track for קרן השתלמות shows the lowest fee on the list, 0.48% "מהחיסכון". מנורה is right behind at 0.49%. Fairly sure, though I can't tell you what that is in shekels.

stuck.where: Line under the filters, "המסלולים מסודרים לפי דמי הניהול מהחיסכון, מהיקר לזול"
stuck.why: At first I thought מור at the top, 0.7%, was the best one. Then I saw it's sorted from most expensive to cheapest, so I had to scroll to the bottom to find the cheapest.
Where the fee should be it says "עוד לא דווח" with an orange warning sign, and it shows only 40% מניות. I didn't know if it really is an S&P track or if it's cheaper, so I left it out.
The header says 12 tracks, but I only counted 11 companies, so maybe I scrolled past one. It's sorted from expensive to cheap, so it probably wasn't the cheapest.

findings.what: Sorted from most expensive to cheapest, so the first row you see (מור, 0.7%) feels like the recommended one. The cheapest is only at the very bottom.
Fees are shown only as percentages. 0.48% vs 0.7% looks like nothing, and nothing tells you what it means in shekels.
A track with "עוד לא דווח" and a warning icon sits under the cheapest one and looks odd (40% מניות on an S&P track)
The header says 12 tracks but I could only count 11 while scrolling
No clear next step for how to switch to the cheapest one
